title: A Phase 1/2 Trial of TER-2013 in Patients with Solid Tumors Harboring AKT/PI3K/PTEN Pathway Alterations
official: A Phase 1/2 Trial of TER-2013 in Patients with Solid Tumors Harboring AKT/PI3K/PTEN Pathway Alterations
summary:
Main objective: Phase 1 Dose Escalation and Phase 1b Sub-study Combination Dose Escalation / Safety Lead-In:
To characterize the safety and tolerability of TER-2013 as monotherapy and in combination with ER antagonists/degraders
To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or maximum administered dose (MAD) of TER-2013 as monotherapy and in combination with fulvestrant

Phase 1 Cohort Expansion and Phase 1b Sub-study Combination Cohort or Dose Expansion:
To evaluate the preliminary clinical activity/efficacy of TER-2013 in advanced solid tumors
To evaluate the preliminary clinical activity/efficacy of TER-2013 in combination with ER antagonists/degraders in HR+/HER2− breast cancer

interventions.name: Fulvestrant Ribosepharm 250 mg Injektionslösung in einer Fertigspritze

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged ≥ 18 years
2. Prior therapies a. Phase 1 Dose Escalation: i. Received standard therapies appropriate for their tumor type and stage and have no standard-of-care therapies remaining, unless contraindicated, intolerable, or patient refused b. Phase 1 Cohort Expansion: i. Ovarian Cancer: received prior platinum-based chemotherapy (adjuvant and/or advanced setting), unless contraindicated, intolerant or patient refused ii. Cervical cancer, squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, lung, and esophagus, and endometrial cancer: received at least 1 prior standard of care therapy in the recurrent or metastatic setting iii. No more than 3 prior lines of treatment in the advanced setting
3. Disease progression on or after the most recent treatment
4. Presence of lesions to be evaluated per RECIST v1.1: a. Dose Escalation: measurable or evaluable disease b. Cohort Expansion: measurable disease
5. Estimated life expectancy ≥ 12 weeks
6. Prothrombin time (PT) or International Normalized Ratio (INR) ≤ 1.5 × ULN; if receiving anticoagulant therapy, PT or activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) is within therapeutic range
7. Toxicity from previous anticancer therapy must be resolved to Grade ≤1 or baseline
8. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1
9. Adequate bone marrow, renal and hepatic funtions
10. Able to swallow capsules or tablets
11. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) or men whose partner is a WOCBP agree to use contraception while participating in this study and for the periods defined in Section 5.3.1 of the protocol following termination of study treatment
12. Histologically confirmed diagnosis of: a. Phase 1 Dose Escalation: solid tumor malignancy harboring an eligible AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway alteration detected in tumor tissue or ctDNA by a Sponsor-approved test; AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway alteration not required, but highly desirable, for HR+ breast cancer b. Phase 1 Cohort Expansion: i. Cohort 1: high-grade serous ovarian/primary peritoneal/fallopian tube carcinoma (“ovarian cancer”), cervical cancer, or squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, lung, or esophagus harboring an eligible AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway alteration detected in tumor tissue or ctDNA by a Sponsor-approved test ii. Cohort 2: endometrial adenocarcinoma harboring an eligible AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway alteration detected in tumor tissue or ctDNA by a Sponsor-approved test c. Phase 2: TBD
13. Eligible AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway alterations: a. Nonsynonymous PIK3CA alterations including mutations that result in an amino acid substitution at kinase domain residues H1047 or G1049, or helical domain/other (non-kinase domain) residues G106, N345, C420, E542, E545, or Q546 b. AKT1 E17K c. PTEN i. Annotated functional mutations C124S/R, G129E/V/R, R130Q/G/L/P, C136R, K342N ii. Homozygous deletion iii. Any nonsense, frameshift, or splice mutation, or gene rearrangement predicted to result in loss of function or expression of PTEN iv. No PTEN expression by IHC. Other potentially functional mutations may be eligible after discussion with the Sponsor and approval by the Medical Monitor
14. Metastatic or locally advanced, unresectable disease
15. No available treatment with curative intent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known EGFR, KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, or BRAF oncogenic-driver co-mutation with PI3K/AKT/PTEN alteration; in some cases, patients may be permitted after discussion with the Sponsor and approved by the Medical Monitor
2. Clinically significant abnormalities of glucose metabolism (defined by a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus type 1 or 2 requiring insulin treatment, or glycated hemoglobin A1c ≥ 8.0% [64 mmol/mol])
3. Active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis
4. Known hemolysis disorder
5. Known or suspected presence of another malignancy that could be mistaken for the malignancy under study during disease assessments, or which is considered clinically significant in the opinion of the Investigator or Medical Monitor
6. Known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or acute or chronic hepatitis B or C infection, with exceptions as noted in the protocol
7. Malabsorption syndrome, nausea and vomiting uncontrolled by medication, or disease significantly affecting gastrointestinal function likely to interfere with the delivery, absorption, or metabolism of TER-2013
8. Pregnant or breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant or breast feed during the study  or within 6 months after last dose of TER-2013 or 24 months after last dose of fulvestrant  (refer to local prescribing information for FASLODEX)
9. Presence of a medical or psychiatric condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, makes the patient inappropriate for inclusion in this study or could interfere with obtaining patient informed consent
10. Ongoing systemic infection requiring parental treatment with antibiotic, antiviral, or antifungal treatment. Note: Prophylactic treatment is not excluded
11. Any of the following cardiac abnormalities: a. Symptomatic or uncontrolled atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmia within 6 months prior to first dose of study drug b. Congestive heart failure ≥ New York Heart Association Class 3 within 6 months prior to first dose of study drug c. Unstable angina pectoris or new-onset angina within the last 3 months or myocardial infarction within the past 6 months prior to the first dose of study drug d. Prolonged QTcF ≥ 450 milliseconds or medical or immediate family history of congenital Long QT Syndrome
12. Arterial or venous thrombotic or embolic events such as cerebrovascular accident (including transient ischemic attacks), deep vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism within 3 months prior to first dose of study drug (except for adequately treated catheter-related venous thrombosis occurring >1 month prior to first dose of study drug)
13. History of significant hemoptysis or hemorrhage within 4 weeks prior to first dose of study drug
14. Prior therapy a. Phase 1 Dose Escalation: AKT inhibitor; in some cases, patients may be permitted after discussion with Sponsor and approved by the Medical Monitor b. Phase 1 Cohort Expansion: AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway inhibitor
15. Prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy, anticancer agent, investigational agent, or tumor embolization within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug Note: Patients with prostate cancer may continue androgen deprivation therapy with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)/luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) agonist/antagonists as long as there has been no change in this treatment within 60 days of first dose of study drug and no planned change in treatment.
16. Palliative radiotherapy within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug
17. Major surgical procedure, including that for cancer treatment, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days before the first dose of study drug or anticipation of need for major surgical procedure during the course of the study. Placement of a vascular access device or minor surgery is permitted within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug (provided that the wound is adequately healed).
